s1.title: Understanding the origin of a couple's problem
s1.p1: Before trying to resolve a conflict, it's essential to understand where it really comes from. Often, what we think is the problem is just the tip of the iceberg.
s1.h3_1: The most common causes of couple conflicts
s1.p2: Couple arguments rarely come from nowhere. Behind every conflict there's usually an unexpressed or unmet need. Poor communication tops the list: we think we understand each other, but we often speak two different languages.
s1.p3: Then comes the lack of time spent together, different views on money, children's education, or life projects. Not to mention the small daily frustrations that accumulate silently until they explode over something trivial.
s1.h3_2: Why the same arguments keep coming back
s1.p4: Feel like you're replaying the same scene? That's normal. Recurring arguments signal that the real problem has never been addressed. We solve the symptom, not the cause. It's like putting a bandage on an infected wound: it relieves for a moment, but comes back.
s1.p5: Until each person's deep needs are identified and acknowledged, the same pattern repeats endlessly.

s2.title: How to resolve a couple's problem permanently
s2.h3_1: Identify the real problem (beyond the argument)
s2.p1: Next time you argue about dishes, ask yourself: are the plates really the problem? Probably not. It might be a feeling of not being supported, carrying too much mental load, or not feeling valued.
s2.p2: The real problem always hides behind the apparent argument. Finding it is already half the journey.
s2.h3_2: Express emotions without escalating the conflict
s2.p3: Saying what you feel without accusing the other is an art. The secret? Talk about yourself. "I feel hurt when..." rather than "You always make me...". This nuance changes everything.
s2.p4: Your partner no longer feels attacked and can truly listen. Your emotions deserve to be heard, but how you express them determines whether they will be.
s2.p5: Listening isn't waiting for your turn to speak. It's truly trying to understand what the other person is experiencing, even if you disagree.
s2.p6: Focus on their words, their emotion. Rephrase what you understood. This simple practice can transform an argument into a real conversation.

s3.title: 10 tips for resolving a couple's problem

tips.h: Communicate at the right time, not in the heat of emotion
tips.p: Timing is crucial. Bringing up a sensitive topic when you're exhausted, angry, or rushed guarantees an argument. Wait for the right moment: when you're both available, calm, and ready to really talk.

tips.h: Talk about yourself without accusing the other
tips.p: Replace "you" with "I". Instead of "You never listen to me," try "I feel ignored when I speak and you look at your phone." The message gets through without putting the other on the defensive.

tips.h: Learn to listen without preparing your response
tips.p: We all have this tendency: while the other talks, we're already preparing our counterargument. Make the conscious effort to listen until the end, to understand, before responding.

tips.h: Accept that the other may feel differently
tips.p: Two people can live the same situation and feel completely different things. Neither is wrong. Accepting this reality means stopping trying to convince the other that their perception is false.
"You always do that," "You never pay attention"... These words are relationship bombs. They exaggerate reality and put the other in an impossible position. Stay factual.

tips.h: Seek a solution rather than someone to blame
tips.p: The goal of a couple's discussion isn't to win or prove the other wrong. It's to find together how to feel better. Ask yourself: "How do we prevent this from happening again?"

tips.h: Respect each other's needs and boundaries
tips.p: Everyone has their own needs: for solitude, for expression, for affection, for financial security... Knowing and respecting them is the foundation of a healthy relationship.

tips.h: Take breaks when the discussion gets too tense
tips.p: Sometimes, the best thing is to stop. When voices rise and words go beyond thoughts, suggest a break. It's not running from the problem, it's protecting it from a destructive escalation.
Small frustrations kept to yourself end up forming a mountain. Learn to express your feelings as they come, before they become resentment.

tips.h: Get help when dialogue goes in circles
tips.p: Recognizing you can't do it alone isn't failure, it's a sign of maturity. An outside perspective can unlock situations that seemed impossible to resolve.

s4.title: Mistakes to avoid when trying to resolve a couple conflict

items.h: Trying to be right rather than understood
items.p1: It's the classic trap. We so want to prove we're right that we forget what's essential: understanding each other.
items.p2: The relational victory is when both feel heard.

items.p1: Your partner doesn't necessarily expect you to solve their problem. Sometimes they just need to be heard, understood, supported.
items.p2: This simple question can change everything.

s5.title: Can you really resolve a couple's problem alone?
s5.h3_1: The limits of discussions between two
s5.p1: When emotionally involved, it's hard to be objective. Each person sees the situation through their own lens, wounds, and experiences.
s5.h3_2: When and why an outside perspective can help
s5.p2: A neutral third party sees what you no longer see. They can rephrase, decode, and highlight repetitive patterns.

s6.title: Resolve a couple's problem with artificial intelligence
s6.h3_1: How AI analyzes a couple's argument
s6.p1: Our AI analyzes your situation methodically and impartially. It examines the context, each person's arguments, and identifies friction points.
s6.h3_2: How AI can help communicate better
s6.p2: AI puts words to what's sometimes hard to express. It rephrases each person's position clearly and factually.
s6.h3_3: The benefits of a neutral tool for calming conflicts
s6.p3: When emotions take over, having a neutral referee changes everything. AI doesn't judge, doesn't take sides, and isn't influenced by tears or outbursts.

s7.title: How to use our tool to resolve a couple's problem
s7.p1: The first step is crucial: describe the context neutrally and factually. The more objective you are, the more relevant the analysis will be.
s7.p2: Then each person expresses their version. The AI will consider both perspectives to understand the conflict dynamic.
s7.p3: Finally, you receive a complete analysis: the severity level, resolution chances, responsibility distribution, and above all concrete advice for moving forward.
